title: Notes on long-tail behaviors in low-bit inference
content:
Quick context / goal:
- Working notes on weird, long-tail failure modes when running models at 4-bit/3-bit (per-channel/q8x) in our Private/Dedicated infra. Trying to capture observed behaviors, hypothesize causes, and outline tests to reproduce and mitigate.

High-level summary of observations (so far):
- Increased micro-hallucinations at long context boundaries (>4096 tokens) that are not present in fp16 baseline. These are small factual errors, often tied to rare tokens or entity names.
- Tokenization boundary sensitivity: minor prompt edits (adding a space or switching punctuation) sometimes flip decoding into repetition loops under 4-bit runs.
- Degredation in numerical stability for arithmetic-like prompts (few-shot addition/subtraction sequences) — errors scale non-linearly with sequence length.
- Heavier tail-probability mass on a few tokens during autoregressive steps (squeezed softmax shape) causing mode-collapse-like repetition in greedy/beam decoding.
- Beam search amplifies artifacts (beams converge to the same wrong phrase) more often under quantized kernels.

Setup notes (where experiments ran):
- Model baseline: LLaMA-2-13B fp16 (our private build), compared to LLaMA-2-13B quantized to 4-bit (GPTQ-like pipeline) and an 8-bit roundtrip.
- Runtime: Redwood Private, dedicated vGPU pool (A10G equiv), custom kernel path: k8.2-lowbit-2027-01.
- Common config: temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, max_new_tokens=1024, batch size variable (1/4/8).
- Eval harness: mix of synthetic arithmetic prompts, truncated Wikipedia paragraphs, and Redwood internal prompt suites (JIRA-MLINF-412).

Detailed failure-mode examples (copy-paste from logs):
- Example A (long-context): seed prompt includes a timeline with 7 historical events. At token ~512 we see: "In 1845, the company was founded by..." -> repeats "the company was founded by" 4 times and then stops. On fp16: no repeat.
- Example B (token boundary): prompt ends with "Dr." vs "Dr" — quantized run produces: "Dr. Dr. Dr." repeated in generation, while fp16 completes normally.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization-induced narrowing of logits distribution: low-bit transforms reduce dynamic range causing high-probability mass to concentrate. Leads to greedy sticking.
2) KV cache accumulation rounding: after many steps, small round-off errors on key/query matrix matmul accumulate and shift attention weights unpredictably at tail positions.
3) Kernel-specific softmax approximation differences (approx exp/softmax table) — our low-bit kernels might be using approximation that diverges for extreme logits.
4) Interaction with tokenizer: subword segmentation shifts rarely seen subwords into slightly different logits that get amplified by quantization noise.

Quick checks to run (prioritized):
- Reproduce one concrete seed deterministically across fp16 / 8-bit / 4-bit with same RNG and exact prompt. Log full softmax vectors for the first 200 tokens to see when distributions diverge. (TODO: add to eval harness + storage)
- Float-preserving run: run quantized forward but compute final softmax in fp32 (if possible) to see if post-softmax re-normalization helps.
- KV-cache drift test: run identical prompt twice on same quantized model back-to-back; does second run drift more? If yes, suggests accumulated in-kernel state or RNG instability.
- Decoding-resilience test: try nucleus decoding (top_p=0.8) and temperature sweeps to see if artifacts reduce — but can't rely on sampling changes for production.

Measurement plan / metrics to capture:
- Divergence step: first token index where top-1 differs from fp16 baseline.
- Softmax entropy and top-5 mass distribution over time.
- Frequency of repetition events (>=3 repeats) per 1k tokens.
- Numeric RMS difference on logits between quant and fp16 (logged per layer if feasible).

Quick experiment notes (results so far):
- Batch size effect: larger batch sizes (>=4) increase chance of repeat events in quantized runs — possibly a batching kernel race or fused-kernel precision tradeoff.
- Temp=0.0 (greedy) shows the worst divergence; sampling with temp=0.7 reduces repetition but increases hallucination variance.
- 8-bit runs are close to fp16 in behavior; primary delta is with 4-bit and below.

Actionable mitigations to try (small experiments):
- Softmax smoothing: add a tiny epsilon or temperature adjustment pre-softmax in the low-bit kernel. Cheap to test as a shim in the runtime.
- Periodic re-centering of KV cache: after every N tokens recompute keys/values in higher precision (expensive but try N=128).
- Hybrid decoding: for the first long-context tokens use fp16 compute then switch to low-bit for steady-state.
- Prompt engineering guardrails: auto-insert trailing non-breaking space or zero-width char to avoid token boundary triggers (hacky but cheap).

Outstanding questions / unknowns:
- Is this more hardware-specific (A10g vs H100) or kernel-version specific? Need cross-run on an H100 cluster.
- How do model architecture differences (RoPE vs ALiBi) interact with quant drift at long context?
- Any prior art: do ZeroQuant/GPTQ papers mention KV drift? I couldn't find explicit KV drift analysis — need to search deeper.

Follow-ups and next steps (2-week sprint):
- Week 1: deterministically reproduce 3 canonical failure seeds and capture full token-level diagnostic traces (logits, entropy, attn norms). Assigned: me + Evan.
- Week 2: test mitigations locally (softmax tweak, KV re-centering) and run on one H100 pod. Capture cost/latency impact. Assigned: Hannah + infra.
- Create a short internal write-up (1 pager) summarizing root-cause guesses and mitigation effectiveness for eng-runtime review. (Target: 2027-03-05)

Notes to self / stray thoughts:
- Might be worth adding a small suite of "stability prompts" to Redwood Optimize so customers can validate quantized variants on their own prompts.
- If mitigation is kernel-level, consider adding a runtime switch: "stability_mode": true for long-context sessions.

References and reading list (quick):
- GPTQ: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155 (look at weight grouping notes)
- On quantization noise and attention: internal Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABC123/thread-1642
- Very relevant: "BitNet" style error accumulation papers (TODO: clean up links)

End of scratchpad. Will iterate as experiments land.

-- sofia
